tools.name: Perplexity Computer
tools.description: An outcome-driven workspace combining research, code, browser work, and multiple AI models.
tools.best: Research-to-deliverable work across tools.
tools.watch: Execution usage is not equivalent to a token price. Review action permissions and current plan limits.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: A unified model API with provider selection and fallback routing.
tools.best: Trying and routing across model providers.
tools.watch: Model and provider choices affect price, privacy, availability, and supported parameters.

tools.name: Runware
tools.description: A generation API spanning images, video, audio, text, and 3D.
tools.best: Building multi-modal media generation into a product.
tools.watch: Not the same product layer as a general LLM gateway; endpoint and model capabilities differ.

tools.name: Manus
tools.description: An autonomous agent that plans and executes tasks in an internet-connected sandbox.
tools.best: Handing off a multi-step task end to end.
tools.watch: Validate connectors, task reliability, permissions, and current plan limits for your exact job.

tools.name: Claude Cowork
tools.description: Multi-step knowledge work across files and connected tools, with work returned for review.
tools.best: Documents, analysis, and work in approved local folders.
tools.watch: Local computer access requires desktop; only the folders and tools you approve are accessible.

tools.name: ChatGPT agent
tools.description: A virtual-computer agent for research, website interaction, and multi-step tasks.
tools.best: Moving from research to actions on websites.
tools.watch: The reviewed launch article is historical. Confirm current regional availability and limits.

tools.name: OpenClaw
tools.description: An open-source assistant on your machine, connected to chat apps, files, and tools.
tools.billing: Software is free; model / hosting costs separate
tools.best: A personal assistant with local state and configurable models.
tools.watch: Local state does not guarantee local inference. Scope shell, browser, and messaging permissions carefully.

tools.name: Gamut
tools.description: A shared workspace for AI teammates that use tools, run schedules, and build apps.
tools.best: Shared team agents with schedules and approvals.
tools.watch: Review sandbox scope, approval rules, model costs, and hosted versus self-hosted operation.

tools.name: Genspark
tools.description: An AI workspace for creating slides, documents, media, code, and dashboards.
tools.best: Creating work products in an all-in-one workspace.
tools.watch: The reviewed homepage gives broad scope, not a complete execution or integration specification.

tools.name: Gemini Deep Research
tools.description: Plans web and selected Workspace research, then synthesizes a structured report.
tools.best: Source-driven research with optional Gmail, Drive, and Chat context.
tools.watch: Primarily a research workflow, not a like-for-like substitute for arbitrary computer execution.

tools.name: Requesty
tools.description: A unified LLM gateway with routing, observability, and provider management.
tools.billing: Verify current gateway and usage fees
tools.best: Managing production LLM traffic and provider flexibility.
tools.watch: Check routing policies, provider coverage, and the handling of upstream credentials.

tools.name: Vercel AI Gateway
tools.description: One API for models, provider routing, and fallbacks in the Vercel ecosystem.
tools.best: Adding multi-provider AI to a Vercel application.
tools.watch: Check the specific model, endpoint, credits, and BYOK conditions rather than assuming universal parity.

tools.name: NanoGPT
tools.description: Multi-model access for chat, writing, coding, and media, with a developer API.
tools.best: Exploring many models through one account.
tools.watch: Automatic provider failover is not confirmed by the reviewed overview.

tools.name: Portkey
tools.description: An AI gateway with routing, fallbacks, monitoring, and governance.
tools.best: Operating and observing multi-provider AI applications.
tools.watch: A gateway does not eliminate upstream bills. Confirm the deployment and feature tier you need.

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: A model proxy that normalizes API calls, routes requests, and tracks usage.
tools.best: Controlling a multi-provider proxy in your own infrastructure.
tools.watch: Self-hosting adds operational work; compatible APIs still have provider-specific differences.

tools.name: Cloudflare AI Gateway
tools.description: Observes and controls AI calls with logging, caching, rate limits, and fallbacks.
tools.best: Adding a control layer around existing model providers.
tools.watch: This is not Workers AI. Model inference and gateway controls are different layers.

tools.name: Hugging Face Inference Providers
tools.description: A unified proxy and token for multiple hosted model providers and tasks.
tools.billing: Pay as you go; no extra provider markup stated
tools.best: Using the Hugging Face ecosystem across providers.
tools.watch: OpenAI-compatible endpoint is for chat; other tasks use inference clients. Coverage varies by provider.

tools.name: fal.ai
tools.description: Hosted generative-media models and infrastructure for creative applications.
tools.best: Shipping media generation with a broad model selection.
tools.watch: Check model licenses, queue behavior, output settings, and custom deployment terms.

tools.name: Replicate
tools.description: Run published models, fine-tune supported models, or deploy your own.
tools.best: Prototyping with a model library and custom deployments.
tools.watch: Billing units and startup behavior vary by model and deployment; compare the same settings.

tools.name: Together AI
tools.description: Hosted model inference with serverless, dedicated, and customization options.
tools.best: Open-model applications with a path to customization.
tools.watch: OpenAI-compatible capabilities vary. Video uses a Together-native endpoint.

tools.name: Fireworks AI
tools.description: A model inference platform with deployment and fine-tuning capabilities.
tools.best: Moving open-model workloads into production.
tools.watch: Do not treat vendor performance claims as your benchmark; test your model, region, and concurrency.

tools.name: DeepInfra
tools.description: Hosted LLMs and APIs for embeddings, image generation, speech, and more.
tools.best: Simple hosted access to open models.
tools.watch: OpenAI-compatible chat is documented; other tasks may use different API shapes.

tools.name: Groq
tools.description: Hosted LLM inference with an OpenAI-compatible interface.
tools.best: Evaluating latency-sensitive text applications.
tools.watch: Check current model choices, token limits, and sustained throughput using your own workload.

tools.name: Cerebras Inference
tools.description: Wafer-scale model inference with API and dedicated-capacity options.
tools.best: Evaluating low-latency coding, reasoning, and agents.
tools.watch: API is mostly OpenAI compatible, not universally identical. Benchmark your actual requests.

tools.name: Novita AI
tools.description: An AI platform combining model APIs and GPU infrastructure.
tools.best: Exploring model APIs alongside GPU capacity.
tools.watch: Product breadth is not API parity. Verify each model and deployment's capabilities and terms.

tools.name: Nebius Token Factory
tools.description: An open-model inference API with dedicated endpoints and post-training options.
tools.best: Open-model serving with dedicated and customization paths.
tools.watch: Validate model availability, service region, and post-training requirements before committing.

tools.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
tools.description: Runs a curated model catalog on Cloudflare's serverless GPU network.
tools.billing: Pay for use; free / paid plans
tools.best: Adding model inference to Cloudflare applications.
tools.watch: Model catalog and task limits differ from a general GPU host; AI Gateway is a separate product.

tools.name: Modal
tools.description: Run your own Python code, model inference, batch jobs, and training on serverless compute.
tools.best: Custom models and bursty Python or GPU workloads.
tools.watch: You own more deployment decisions. Include cold starts, storage, idle settings, and maintenance in estimates.

tools.name: Baseten
tools.description: Deploy and optimize open, custom, and fine-tuned models on managed or private infrastructure.
tools.best: Production custom-model serving and dedicated workloads.
tools.watch: Infrastructure and optimization are a different buying decision from a model-routing gateway.

tools.name: Runpod
tools.description: GPU Pods, serverless workers, and public model endpoints for AI workloads.
tools.billing: Serverless per second; other products vary
tools.best: GPU deployment, ComfyUI, and custom inference workers.
tools.watch: OpenAI-style chat requires the relevant worker, such as vLLM; not every endpoint is compatible.

tools.name: Amazon Bedrock
tools.description: Foundation models and tools for production AI applications and agents inside AWS.
tools.best: AI applications within an AWS governance environment.
tools.watch: Region, model, guardrails, and adjacent AWS service charges need separate review.

tools.name: Vertex AI / Model Garden
tools.description: Discover, customize, and deploy Google and partner models on Google Cloud.
tools.best: Google Cloud applications and custom model deployment.
tools.watch: Open-model endpoints incur compute charges; deployment, tuning, and managed APIs have different cost structures.

tools.name: Azure AI Foundry
tools.description: An Azure platform bringing model catalogs, agents, tools, and governance together.
tools.best: AI applications inside an Azure management environment.
tools.watch: Product naming and availability evolve. Check deployment-specific model, region, and network controls.

tools.name: OpenAI API
tools.description: Direct access to OpenAI text, vision, image, audio, and agent-building capabilities.
tools.best: Using OpenAI models and native endpoint features directly.
tools.watch: Model-specific API capabilities and separate media billing require a workload-level comparison.

tools.name: Anthropic API
tools.description: Direct Claude access for text, vision, reasoning, code, and tool use.
tools.best: Building directly on Claude's model and agent capabilities.
tools.watch: Vision input is not image generation. Direct prompting is not the same product as Cowork.

tools.name: Mistral API
tools.description: Mistral's developer platform for language, multimodal, OCR, and audio applications.
tools.best: Direct Mistral usage, document workflows, and transcription.
tools.watch: Task-specific services have different endpoints and terms; confirm residency rather than assuming it.

tools.name: Cursor
tools.description: A coding environment with agents that search, edit, build, and test software.
tools.best: Daily software development with agent-assisted editing.
tools.watch: Agent scope and data access differ by surface; review repository permissions and model usage.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.description: Reads codebases, edits files, runs commands, and integrates with development tools.
tools.best: Agentic coding in existing repositories and developer workflows.
tools.watch: Local and cloud surfaces have different access. Commands and external actions need permission controls.

tools.name: OpenAI Codex
tools.description: A coding tool for understanding projects, building features, reviewing code, and fixing failures.
tools.best: Delegating implementation, debugging, and code review.
tools.watch: Confirm the current execution surface, plan limits, and repository permissions for your workflow.

tools.name: Lovable
tools.description: A natural-language platform for building, iterating on, and deploying full-stack web applications.
tools.best: Going from an app idea to an editable, published prototype.
tools.watch: Budget separately for generation, runtime services, security review, and production QA.

tools.name: n8n
tools.description: A visual workflow builder mixing integrations, code, and AI agents.
tools.best: Repeatable workflows with visibility and infrastructure control.
tools.watch: Self-hosted does not mean all model calls stay local. Review node secrets, retries, and approval steps.

tools.name: Make
tools.description: A visual platform for connecting apps, data, models, and agentic workflows.
tools.best: Visual business processes and cross-app automations.
tools.watch: Check execution units, loops, third-party model bills, and failure handling for your scenario.

tools.name: Zapier
tools.description: App-triggered workflows and agents across a large integration ecosystem.
tools.best: Connecting business applications with trigger-based workflows.
tools.watch: Workflow steps, AI usage, and connected services are not interchangeable billing units.

tools.name: Lindy
tools.description: An AI teammate for connected business tools, recurring jobs, and team work.
tools.best: Operational assistants across email, CRM, meetings, and chat.
tools.watch: Permissions, browser support, and pooled-credit rules depend on the plan and workspace setup.

tools.name: Midjourney
tools.description: A prompt-driven creative image generation service.
tools.best: Hands-on image exploration and visual direction.
tools.watch: A creative app is not automatically a general-purpose public generation API. Check rights and current access terms.

tools.name: Krea
tools.description: A visual creative suite for generating, editing, and enhancing images, video, and 3D.
tools.best: Iterative visual work across multiple creative models.
tools.watch: Model access, output rights, concurrency, and compute allowances vary by plan.

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.description: Voice and audio tools, APIs, and conversational agents for speech-led experiences.
tools.best: Voiceovers, transcription, dubbing, and voice agents.
tools.watch: Review voice consent, commercial rights, model capabilities, and the billing unit for each service.

tools.name: Runway
tools.description: A creative platform and developer API for generating and editing video, images, and audio.
tools.best: Video-led creative production and media workflows.
tools.watch: App subscriptions and developer API access are separate surfaces; verify the model and usage terms.
